speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work is reassuring; your white blood cell count is normal, which makes a severe bacterial infection less likely. Given the combination of fever, headache, rhinorrhea, and a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, could you describe the appearance of the rash in more detail—does it have any blisters, peeling, or a specific pattern?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola)

The progression from an upper respiratory prodrome to a rash starting on the face and spreading to the trunk and extremities, while sparing the perioral area, is highly characteristic of measles. I am requesting images of the rash to confirm the findings before finalizing the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Rash
